justification: A 22,007-row production write that NARROWS what a property is shown. Every other change today widened applicability or corrected a false claim; this one removes provisions from result sets, and hiding a binding control is the failure mode that matters. It also changes user-facing copy on the assessment page.

falsifiable_check.command: SELECT coalesce(v2_zone_source,'(NULL)'), count(*) FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE is_current AND v2_is_actionable AND source_council IN ('marrickville','ashfield','leichhardt') GROUP BY 1;  -- plus: python -m pytest tests/test_applicability_slug_docids.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The predicted distribution was stated BEFORE the write: config_all 7,761, config_specific 815, no_config 1,278. It fails if those counts differ materially, if any row carries a narrowed zone set while v2_zone_source is still 'no_config' (which would mean it was narrowed without a config matching — a guess), or if any written zone code is absent from lep_zone_coverage for Inner West. All three were run after the write: distribution matched exactly, guessed-narrowing count 0, invalid codes 0. The test suite additionally fails if a resolver returns a key the config does not declare.

pre_impl.existing_data: 107 distinct document_ids / 9,854 served rows / 22,007 total rows across the three councils, enumerated in full rather than sampled. Config key vocabularies read directly: MARRICKVILLE_CONFIG parts + precincts, ASHFIELD_CONFIG chapters + chapter_f_parts, LEICHHARDT_CONFIG parts. Zone codes cross-checked against lep_zone_coverage for Inner West.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The tracker said the section code lives in ref_number and the matchers should be taught to read it, implying a signature change. Reading the real data showed the part is already in the document_id as a slug, so no extra field and no signature change was needed. Second mismatch: I expected 9,854 rows to narrow. Only 815 narrow on zones and 882 on dev types; 7,673 resolve to configs that themselves say ALL, so for those the value is unchanged and only the provenance improves from unattributable to attributable.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new surface. Slug resolution was added inside the three existing config getters, tried before the legacy verbose patterns, which are retained for any older document_id. The re-tag script exists because enrichment/pipeline.py::run_applicability_tagging only revisits rows WHERE v2_applicable_zones IS NULL and would skip every affected row; its safety shape is copied from scripts/backfill_invalid_zone_codes.py.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No external API is called. The only source is the local DCP config files plus lep_zone_coverage, read read-only for verification. If a config file were unreadable the tagger raises at import and the re-tag script never reaches its write phase; if lep_zone_coverage were empty the standing zone-validity gate reports unverifiable rather than clean, which is the documented three-state.
pre_impl.frontend_type: The narrowed arrays cross into TypeScript as v2_applicable_zones and v2_applicable_dev_types on the provision rows. Both were already string[] | null and neither changed shape, so no boundary type moved. The one new frontend value is anyDevTypeSpecific, a boolean derived in-component from those arrays with an Array.isArray guard, so a null or absent field reads false rather than throwing.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: The expensive failure is a provision that applies being hidden from a property, because the user would never know it was missing — the opposite direction is only noise. Mitigated by refusing to resolve any config key the council has not declared, which leaves 1,278 served rows deliberately at ALL/no_config, and by verifying after the write that zero rows were narrowed while still recording no_config. Visibly, a Marrickville dwelling-house scope now excludes the commercial and industrial parts; the scope copy states that some provisions are filtered rather than claiming none are.

functions.name: _marrickville_slug_key
functions.input: a slug-form document_id such as part4_s1_low_density or part9_p47_victoria_road
functions.output: a tuple of the entry kind and the config key, only when that key is declared in MARRICKVILLE_CONFIG
functions.if_none: returns None for any slug whose derived key the config does not declare, so the row stays ALL with source no_config rather than being narrowed on a guess

functions.name: _ashfield_slug_key
functions.input: a slug-form document_id such as chapter_e1_heritage or chapter_f_part_7
functions.output: the chapter or chapter-F part key when ASHFIELD_CONFIG declares it
functions.if_none: chapter_e2_haberfield returns None on purpose because no Chapter E2 is declared; its 118 rows stay ALL rather than inheriting another chapter's zones

functions.name: _leichhardt_slug_key
functions.input: a slug-form document_id such as part_c_s2_urban_character or part_f_food
functions.output: the part key, preferring the more specific Section form before the bare part
functions.if_none: appendices, technical manuals and amendments return None and stay ALL, because they are not parts

functions.name: build_plan
functions.input: an open read cursor over the three councils' rows
functions.output: the rows whose tag values change, the rows whose provenance alone changes, and the predicted distribution
functions.if_none: an empty plan writes nothing; the script is dry-run by default so a wrong plan cannot reach the database without an explicit flag

values.value: v2_applicable_zones and v2_applicable_dev_types for 1,928 rows, plus provenance for all 22,007
values.read_at: planning time from regulatory_provisions, then re-read by the per-row UPDATE guard at write time
values.if_missing: 62 rows hold NULL; the guard uses IS NOT DISTINCT FROM against a coalesced empty array so those rows are updated rather than silently skipped, which a plain equality guard would have done

queries.purpose: read every row for the three councils so the new tag can be computed and compared against what is stored
queries.where_clause: WHERE source_council = ANY(%s) with the three councils bound as a parameter; the UPDATE is separately scoped WHERE id = %s plus a null-safe comparison on both previous values, so no unscoped write is possible

break_it.scenario: A slug is resolved to the nearest available config key, narrowing a provision onto zones the council never assigned it — a hidden control.
break_it.what_happens: Resolution is config-authoritative: a derived key is discarded unless the config declares it. chapter_e2_haberfield (118 rows) and part2_s21 (131 rows) deliberately stay ALL for exactly this reason.
break_it.how: TestNeverInventsAKeyTheConfigLacks asserts each unresolvable case returns None, and asserts the key really is absent from the config first so the test cannot pass for the wrong reason.

break_it.scenario: The matcher fix is wrong and a re-tag writes 9,854 bad rows.
break_it.what_happens: The hundred-row sample was re-run first: Inner West rows resolving went 0/52 to 44/52, and the 8 that still do not resolve are the unmapped documents. Only then was the blast radius computed, and only then the write.
break_it.how: Dry-run is the default and prints the full plan; the plan was reconciled against an independent validation script over all 107 document_ids before --apply.

break_it.scenario: The 62 NULL-valued rows are silently skipped by the concurrency guard, so the write reports success while leaving them untagged.
break_it.what_happens: It would have. The guard was written as `v2_applicable_zones = %s`, and NULL = anything is NULL, so all 62 would have failed the predicate. Found by inspecting the planned values before applying.
break_it.how: Guard rewritten as coalesce(...) IS NOT DISTINCT FROM. The run reported 22,007 updated and 0 skipped, which is how the fix was confirmed rather than assumed.

break_it.scenario: Provisions are narrowed and the assessment page keeps telling users nothing was removed.
break_it.what_happens: It would have. Leichhardt is the sort_only council and its copy asserted 'all N provisions apply regardless of dev type — does not remove any'. Correcting the tagger gave Leichhardt Part F real dev types, making the sentence false for those provisions.
break_it.how: The copy is now derived from the provisions actually loaded (anyDevTypeSpecific) rather than assumed, so it stays true whichever way the corpus goes. This is the DQ-31 lesson applied: an API fix that stops before the UI is invisible.

break_it.scenario: A narrowed row is written with a zone code that does not exist in that LGA, reintroducing DQ-30.
break_it.what_happens: Every code written was checked against lep_zone_coverage for Inner West after the write: E1, E4, MU1, R1, R2, R3, R4 — all present, none retired. The existing zone-validity gate also passes.
break_it.how: The tagger's valid_zones filter from DQ-30 is untouched, and the standing validator was re-run post-write.

break_it.scenario: A count or empty-state elsewhere in the UI breaks when a section shrinks to zero.
break_it.what_happens: Checked rather than assumed: the only provision counts are the export label and the scope copy, both derived from the filtered list. No empty-state assumes ALL, and zero rows hold an empty zone array, which under the live predicate would match no zone at all.
break_it.how: Consumer traced before the write, per the sequence, not after.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest && npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck

break_it.scenario: The provenance flag is computed before the provisions it reads, throwing at render.
break_it.what_happens: It was — anyDevTypeSpecific was inserted at line 355 while allProvisions is declared at 647. TypeScript caught it as a use-before-declaration once node_modules was linked into the worktree.
break_it.how: Moved below its dependency; 0 TS errors. Same ordering mistake as an earlier PR today, which is why the type check was run before committing rather than after.

post_merge.db_reset: Already applied. 22,007 rows updated, 0 skipped. Backup table regulatory_provisions_dq33_backup_20260801 holds all four columns for every touched row; rollback SQL is printed by the script and recorded in the tracker.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open the assessment page for a Marrickville R2 address in DA mode and confirm the commercial and industrial parts no longer appear for a dwelling-house scope, while heritage and the Part 2 general controls still do. Then a Leichhardt address: confirm the scope copy reads the 'small number are written for specific development types' wording rather than 'does not remove any'.
